scenario: It is 1841, and I am the captain of a ship that has just sunk after colliding with a rocky bluff. Survivors managed to escape in two lifeboats. My lifeboat (Lifeboat A) contains me and several other crew members and passengers. It is already at full capacity, and it cannot safely take on any additional people. The other lifeboat (Lifeboat B) contains 21 passengers and crew members. Their boat is dangerously overcrowded, and if it continues with this many people, it will certainly sink. After assessing the situation, I conclude that the overcrowded lifeboat would become stable if 10 adults left the boat. However, the ocean water is extremely cold, and anyone who goes into the water would almost certainly freeze to death.
choice: I decide to ask for 10 passengers to volunteer to go overboard
entities: 1 captain in Lifeboat A,unknown number of other crew members and passengers in Lifeboat A,10 volunteering passengers from Lifeboat B who would go overboard,11 remaining passengers and crew members in Lifeboat B,I
outcomes: Passengers and crew in Lifeboat B feel intense pressure to sacrifice themselves
Conflict and pleading arise in Lifeboat B
Ten adults go into the freezing water
Ten adults die from cold exposure
The remaining 11 people in Lifeboat B avoid immediate sinking from overcrowding
Survivors in both lifeboats experience grief and trauma
